New stuff:
- `?longrest` tracks channels even better. In addition to that, if you go IC to another IC channel while you're resting, you'll get a warning. If you do it again, it'll be counted as interrupting your long rest, with all the usual things that happen like AB shouting at you hours later
- you can also manually decide to interrupt your long rest without doing the spamming elsewhere by `?longrest stop` (or `?longrest cancel` or `?longrest interrupt`, pick whichever's easiest to remember)
- also speaking of long rests, during the intermission the warnings for missing your long rests are switched off, and in a bit I'll switch off the notifications for people coming back from a 24h+ hiatus. Using `?longrest` is still active, if you feel like doing that
- new command: `?timer` lets you set up a custom timer. `?shortrest` is still there working as a timer fixed at 1h
?help timer

?timer
`?timer <duration> [optionally text]`

Set up an arbitrary timer, for the bot to ping you like with short rest.
You specify how many minutes or hours as the duration argument:
- if it's just a number, it's minutes
- for hours, do e.g. `3h`
- for mixed hours and minutes do e.g. `1h15m` or `1h15`
Maximum time is 8h (480 minutes).

so warlock vs cleric, vs paladin is a really nuanced and weird thing..... but basically one way or another you are granted access to raw power, and you shape it.

An eldritch blast can manifest as eye lasers, or finger guns, or spectral arrows fired from a ghostly bow, etc..... its how you shape the power with your will into effect.  Basically all warlock spells would be similar

cleric, a diety is granting you access to divine power, so all the magic should be shaped/flavored based on the god at hand (so for instance if your god is Zeus, then lots of lightning and thunder flavor would be approprate, whereas hephestus, might manifest with the sound of a hammer on anvil or some such.  Clerics devoted to a domain without god, would likely still be flavored on what the core of that domain is)

Paladins are no longer really holy.... instead they are devoted so hard to their oaths, various gods are likely to justgrant them power.  As such the oath would likely flavor the magic (so a summoned steed for oath of vengance might look more like a nightmare, whereas order of nature might be an elk)
